stories.title: Drone strike kills at least 14 at Dnipro railway station
stories.summary: At least 14 people were killed and another 14 injured, including an 11‑year‑old boy, when a Russian jet‑powered drone struck a crowded platform at Dnipro’s main railway station. Ukrainian officials said a passenger train bound for Zaporizhzhia was on the platform at the time. The site has been sealed off as authorities investigate; Russia has not commented and denies targeting civilians.
stories.why: It highlights the risk to civilian transport infrastructure in the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Bitcoin trades near $80,000 after Fed holds rates, signals possibility of further tightening
stories.summary: Bitcoin traded near $80,000 after the US Federal Reserve held interest rates at 3.75%-4%, while the possibility of further tightening weighed on sentiment. Analysts flagged resistance near $81,500-$82,000, citing weak technical indicators and subdued institutional demand.
stories.why: This can affect market expectations, company valuations, sector sentiment or capital flows.

stories.title: India can achieve $1 trillion exports target this fiscal despite global headwinds: Piyush Goyal
stories.summary: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal expressed confidence that India would achieve its $1 trillion exports target in 2026-27 despite global uncertainties. He said nine FTAs could open preferential market access to economies with a combined GDP of $60 trillion.
stories.why: Trade developments can affect currencies, business costs, market access and the external balance of the economies involved.

stories.title: Ambuja Cements profit drops ~90% YoY
stories.summary: Ambuja Cements reported that its net profit for the quarter fell about 90% compared with the same quarter a year earlier. The company said the decline was driven by higher input costs and by a strong profit base in the prior year. No detailed financial figures were provided in the source.
stories.why: The steep earnings drop signals cost pressure in the Indian cement sector and could influence investor sentiment.

stories.title: Finance ministry projects 7.35% GDP growth for India in Q2 FY27
stories.summary: The finance ministry’s nowcasting model estimates that India’s gross domestic product will expand by 7.35% in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027. This follows a 7.8% growth rate in the preceding quarter. The forecast attributes the acceleration to stronger industrial output, higher energy consumption, increased port traffic, rising GST collections and robust automobile sales.
stories.why: The projection signals sustained economic momentum, shaping policy decisions and market expectations.

stories.title: IMF says Super El Niño risks to India’s growth have not yet materialised
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund noted that India remains a major driver of global growth. It warned that weather events such as a Super El Niño pose potential risks, but those risks have not yet materialised. The IMF also raised its growth forecasts for India to 7 % for fiscal years 2027‑28, citing strong domestic demand and a buoyant services sector.
stories.why: The IMF’s assessment can influence confidence in India’s economic data, policy credibility and macroeconomic outlook.

stories.title: Mistral releases weights for its trillion‑parameter open‑source model ML4
stories.summary: French AI company Mistral has released the weights for its trillion‑parameter open‑source model Mistral Large 4 (ML4), nicknamed “Le Chonk,” enabling businesses and governments to download and deploy the system themselves. The launch follows earlier announcements and is framed as a competitive alternative to closed‑model providers, highlighting the advantage of data control for cybersecurity workloads. Mistral says ML4 matches the performance of China’s GLM‑5.3 while using 47 percent fewer tokens per task, making it more economical.
stories.why: It lets organizations run a high‑capacity AI model in‑house, reducing reliance on external providers for sensitive cybersecurity tasks.
